# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_006_page_001.jpg

---

6:1 Hear, therefore, O kings, and understand; learn, O judges of the ends of the earth.

6:2 Give ear, you who rule over multitudes and are proud of many nations.

6:3 For your dominion was given to you from the Lord, and your sovereignty from the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your counsels.

6:4 Because, being servants of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor keep the law, nor walk according to God's will,

6:5 he will come upon you swiftly and terribly; for a severe judgment falls on those in high places.

6:6 For the lowliest man may be pardoned in mercy, but mighty men will be mightily tested.

6:7 For the Lord of all will show no partiality, and will not stand in awe of greatness; for he himself made both small and great, and has equal care for all;

6:8 but a strict inquiry is in store for the powerful.

6:9 To you, therefore, O sovereigns, my words are directed, that you may learn wisdom and not transgress.

6:10 For those who have kept holy things in a holy way will be made holy, and those who have been taught them will find a defense;

6:11 desire therefore my words, long for them, and you will be instructed.

6:12 Wisdom is radiant and unfading, and she is easily perceived by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.

6:13 She hastens to make herself known to those who desire her.

6:14 One who rises early to seek her will have no difficulty, for he will find her sitting at his gates.

6:15 For to think upon her is perfect understanding, and one who is vigilant on her account will soon be free from care;

6:16 for she goes about seeking those worthy of her, and she graciously appears to them on their paths, and meets them in every thought.

6:17 For the beginning of wisdom is the most sincere desire for instruction, and concern for instruction is love of her,

6:18 and love of her is the keeping of her laws, and giving heed to her laws is the assurance of immortality,

6:19 and immortality brings one close to God;

6:20 so then desire for wisdom leads to a kingdom.

6:21 Therefore if you delight in thrones and scepters, O rulers of the peoples, honor wisdom, that you may reign for ever.

6:22 What wisdom is and how she came to be, I will make known to you, and I will not hide mysteries from you; but I will trace her out from the beginning of creation, and bring the knowledge of her into the open, and I will not pass by the truth.

6:23 Neither will I travel with sickly envy, for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom.

6:24 A multitude of wise men is the salvation of the world, and a prudent king is the stability of his people.

6:25 Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will profit.

---

*EMET notes: Chapter 6 is a sorites — a chain argument — linking desire for instruction to love, love to law-keeping, law-keeping to immortality, immortality to nearness to God (vv. 17–20). This is a masterwork of Hellenistic rhetorical logic applied to Jewish wisdom theology. "Radiant and unfading" (v. 12): apaugasma (radiance) and amarantos (unfading) are key terms. Verse 12 introduces Wisdom personified, which will dominate chs. 7–9.*
